supersedes: 1.0 (two people compared by the closeness of their rates, which is sameness)
premise: Align complementary types; do not match. Sameness is sought only where a relationship needs something shared.

validation: Every count answered; 0 is an answer. Each starting age is an age or never.
A starting age cannot be after the current age.
A never relationship clock requires 0 relationships and a longest of 0.
A never sexual clock requires 0 people slept with.
A longest relationship needs at least one relationship.
The longest relationship cannot exceed the time since the first began (half a year of slack).
Couple measures need every role, shape and relationship number answered; no answer is read as a default.

perDirection.supply: E_P(role) * X_P(role) * reach_Q(counterpart) + E_Q(counterpart) * X_Q(counterpart) * reach_P(role)

couple.complement: sum(met) / sum(sought) over all 38 directions; null when nothing is sought
couple.lift: sum(supply) / sum(reach); null reads "nothing sought"; reported, not in Together

items.sexualAppetite: exp(-d^2 / (2 T^2)), d = |log2(perDay_A / perDay_B)|; both zero = 1; one zero = 0

definitions.middle: T = 1 / sqrt(2 ln 1.25): a doubling scores 80
definitions.loose: T = 1 / sqrt(2 ln(1 / 0.9)): a doubling scores 90

spread.tree: couple -> 2 sides -> 19 pairs (9 relationship, 10 sexual) -> 38 directions; mass = met
spread.evenness: J = -sum(p ln p) / ln(number of children) (Pielou 1966)

levels.sides: J over the two sides, each side weighed by its met per direction it holds (18 relationship, 20 sexual), so the halves count alike
levels.pairs: sum over sides of (side share) * J(its pairs)
levels.directions: sum over pairs of (side share) * (pair share within side) * J(its two directions)

spread.spread: (sides + pairs + directions) / 3; null when nothing is met
spread.interpretation: A finite, scale-by-scale reading of the information dimension of a multiplicative cascade (Mandelbrot 1974); exact for a regular cascade that splits the same way at every level. No parameters.

couple.together: 100 * sqrt(complement * accord) * (1 + spread) / 2; null when complement is null

spreadWeight.decidedBy: Claude, delegated by Briar Greenway to research
spreadWeight.derivation: Write the factor as (1 - w) + w S with w the unknown true weight of spread. Under a uniform prior on w (Laplace), the expected factor is the integral from 0 to 1 of ((1 - w) + w S) dw = (1 + S) / 2.
reasons: Direction: the insurance hypothesis (Yachi and Loreau 1999) and multiplexity (Verbrugge 1979) say spread should count.
Floor: single-axis complementarity is associated with satisfaction (Dryer and Horowitz 1997; Markey and Markey 2007), so spread must not zero a couple.
Size: no study measures it; the uniform prior averages over every possible weight.
sameRuleAlsoSets: equal weights of complement and accord in the geometric mean
the two sides as equal halves

spreadWeight.toBeReplacedBy: an estimate of w from outcome data

correction: An earlier draft took Complement from experience and reach alone. Two experienced partners who both wanted a role pairing scored "nothing sought", and experience counted as good, contradicting the principle that experience is neither positive nor negative. Complement now comes from expectation; experience lives in Lift.

Experience Quotients calculator

Two people each answer for themselves. Each gets a reading: REEQ over SEEQ from their counts, and an experience-over-expectation number for relationships and for sex. Together, the calculator shows how their types complement each other, where they need to agree, how widely their complementarity is spread, and any boundaries one has drawn that the other wants to cross. It does not look for people who are the same. The method is set out in the white paper.

For adults only (18 and over). Nothing you type leaves this page and nothing is saved: there is no server, no storage, no cookies and no analytics, and the page is not allowed to make any network request. Closing or reloading the tab erases everything.

    Appetite comparison:

    Together = 100 × √(Complement × Accord) × (1 + Spread) ÷ 2. Complement is how much of what each of you wants in a complementary role the other wants in the counterpart role. Accord is agreement on the things that need to be shared. Spread runs from 0 (all your complementarity sits in one role) to 1 (it is spread evenly across every role and both directions). Boundaries never enter the number; they are listed below so they cannot be averaged away.
